sensitivity._note: The verdict turns on the differential between the half-spread I0 pays on US mega-cap names and the half-spread E0 pays on the LSE-listed UCITS lines. Both are swept rather than assumed.

provenance.basis_note: The register's E0 series is the deployed engine's yfinance_trading_proxy under auto_adjust=True (IUES->XLE, IUUS->XLU, IUCS->XLP, IUFS->XLF; SOXX on itself), NOT the LSE UCITS line the book holds. All income and fee figures here are DIFFERENTIAL adjustments from that register basis to the basis a Singapore-resident individual actually experiences.
known_gaps: iShares fund-level actual withholding suffered is not verified per-fund; the 15% treaty rate is used. Published analogue (Vanguard VUSA FY2014) computed 14.74%.

NEITHER side of the spread differential is verified: no per-sector or named mega-cap bps table for US large caps, and no published spread statistic for any LSE-listed iShares S&P 500 sector UCITS line. Reported as a sweep.

Whether IBKR's per-order minimum applies to FRACTIONAL orders is unresolved and is the largest driver of minimum viable NAV: $150k Fixed / $50k Tiered / $25k fractional, and $200k under the stricter all-in-2x reading.
Which IBKR LSE schedule applies to the USD-denominated UCITS lines, and the USD/GBP rate for its minimum, are assumptions. The percentage leg dominates, so the minimum matters little.
IBKR Tiered third-party pass-through fees are disclosed but not modelled.
SOXX AUM disagrees across sources by more than 2x ($20.6bn fact sheet 2026-03-31, $45.1bn Morningstar, $47.8bn AAII). Not used in this model, but noted.

rejected_estimator.estimator: Corwin & Schultz (2012) daily high-low spread estimator
rejected_estimator.what_it_returned: half-spreads of 11.97 bps (utilities) and 8.82 bps (staples) against 2.20 bps (energy) and 1.83 bps (semiconductors) on the PARTIAL-5 held names
rejected_estimator.verdict: REJECTED, not adopted and not bias-corrected
rejected_estimator.why: The literature documents this as the estimator's principal failure mode. Corwin & Schultz's own Table 6 reports correlation with the true effective spread falling from 70% in the low-cap decile to 18% in the high-market-cap decile - close to uninformative for exactly the S&P 500 mega-caps held here. Tremacoldi-Rossi & Irwin (2022) prove the bias is DECREASING IN THE TRUE SPREAD and simulate a true 0.1% spread reading as roughly 1.3% under ideal conditions; their 2009-2013 sample shows a 1.80% average CS estimate against a 0.85% true effective spread.
rejected_estimator.mechanism_correction: The first reading of this project's own output attributed the pattern to a LOW-VOLATILITY bias, since the high readings landed on utilities and staples. That is not the mechanism. The dominant driver is the small TRUE spread of a liquid mega-cap; volatility enters only above roughly sigma/S ~ 4.2 (Tremacoldi-Rossi & Irwin 2022, Proposition 3). The sector pattern is a liquidity artefact, not a volatility one.
rejected_estimator.not_a_fix: Abdi & Ranaldo (2017) close-high-low is the same bias family; their own Table 5 shows proxy quality is worse in the most-liquid effective-spread quintile.
rejected_estimator.recommended_instead: Holden & Jacobsen (2014) effective/quoted spreads from NBBO tick data, or - cheaper and available here - measure the book's own quoted spreads at rebalance time during the T2 shadow.

dividend_basis.why: Conservative: it over-states I0's withholding by treating stock spin-offs as income, penalising the arm under consideration.
dividend_basis.alternative: capitalspecial (TOTALRETURN less CAPITALSPECIAL) - ordinary cash dividends only, which under-states by stripping genuine cash variable dividends.
dividend_basis.neither_is_exact: Withholding is due on cash dividends ordinary and special alike, but not on stock spin-offs, and no Norgate setting splits cash specials from stock specials. Spin-offs in the held set: EQT/Equitrans 2018, DTE/DT Midstream 2021, EXC/Constellation 2022.
dividend_basis.materiality: The two bases differ by about 0.021%/yr on a 0.205%/yr income leg, roughly 0.0014 net Sharpe. Does not move the verdict; a T4 refinement if the margin tightens.

dominant_parameter.finding: E0's own commission is a large term: on IBKR's published LSE Tiered schedule (0.05% of trade value, no maximum) the LSE-listed UCITS legs cost about 0.05% a side, and at 16.6x annual one-way turnover that compounds materially. BOTH arms bear it - I0-PARTIAL5 still holds six sector lines and three broad slices as ETFs - so it is NOT a differential in I0's favour. An earlier vintage of this file claimed it was; that claim was an artefact of assigning commission per ledger rather than per instrument, and is struck.
dominant_parameter.corrected_conclusion: All-in frictions roughly WASH at scale. PARTIAL-5 clears the signed floors; it does not win. Drag is +0.012 at $250k, crosses zero near $350k, and settles near -0.04 to -0.05 at $1m and above - but most of what remains above the crossover is the +0.017 seen-window gross gap that the registration's seen-data caveat bars from counting as evidence. The case for adoption is book structure, not performance.
dominant_parameter.status: Which IBKR LSE schedule applies to the USD-denominated UCITS lines remains unverified. Confirm from actual fills before the T4 verdict.
dominant_parameter.wider_implication: Still stands, and is the larger finding: the register costs E0 at a flat 2 bps. If the LSE schedule is right, the deployed book's true trading cost is far higher, and every WS-series E0 net-Sharpe figure is optimistic. Belongs to the deployed engine, not to WS6b.

defects_found_and_fixed: HIGH: commission assigned per LEDGER not per INSTRUMENT - I0's LSE legs charged the US per-share rate while E0 paid 0.05% on identical orders. Flattered I0 by ~0.020 Sharpe base / ~0.040 at 2x. Fixed via schedule_resolver + venues map; pinned by 5 new tests.
MEDIUM: the promised all-in-2x variant was dead code (a label the loop never produced). Now real - and it bites: $150k FAILS the 0.10 floor at 0.1028 under that reading.
MEDIUM: the 'I0 beats E0 from $250k' narrative was wrong post-fix and leaned on seen-data gross outperformance. Struck.
LOW: SOXX priced off the auto-adjusted proxy panel; its 2024 15:1 split inflated pre-split share counts. Now sourced from Norgate unadjusted.
open_low_severity: us_situs is recorded but the axis is not priced; the T4 record should name it explicitly.
fractional_min_applies is decorative - the fractional treatment is already encoded in that schedule's min_order of 0.01.

scenarios._note: Minimum viable NAV depends on which schedule the book actually trades under. Reported as a bracket, not a point.

venues._note: Commission follows the instrument's listing venue, not the ledger. Verified from etf_registry ishares_region: SOXX is the only US-listed line; the other thirteen are LSE-listed Irish UCITS.
